messages.subject: Re: Overlay images from dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi, sorry for the slow response time. Perhaps you have already figured this out:

To overlay images, you just specify "mz" as a vector, and include "superpose=TRUE".

For example, to recreate the first image from https://ms-imaging.org/wp/imzml/example-files-test/, you would do:

library(Cardinal)

mouse <- readMSIData("/path/to/file.imzML")

image(mouse,
      mz=c(741.5307, 743.5482, 798.541),
      col=c("blue", "red", "green"),
      normalize.image="linear",
      contrast.enhance="suppression",
      superpose=TRUE)

legend("topright",
       fill=c("blue", "red", "green"),
       legend=c(741.5307, 743.5482, 798.541))

Note that you specify "col" instead of "col.regions" to specify categorical rather than continuous color schemes. In the case of overlaid images, Cardinal will automatically add the appropriate alpha levels.

Also, "normalize.image" here is used to rescale the intensities to the same range in order to more easily compare the spatial distributions. Leave it out (or set to "none") to leave the intensities as-is.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Is is possible to perform peak picking with a group of MSImageSet?
messages.subject_clean: Is is possible to perform peak picking with a group of MSImageSet?
messages.body_plain:
You can combine the images beforehand with "combine()" before doing peak-picking. This is the easiest way to get the same peaks for all samples. Note that this requires the original datasets to have the same m/z values. If they don't, you can use reduceDimension() with method="bin" or "resample" to re-bin the datasets to the same m/z values.

Alternatively, you can peak-pick on the datasets individually, and then align them to the same reference when doing peakAlign(). By default, is calculates the local maxima of the mean spectrum of the current dataset to use as a reference, but you could also choose the peaks from one of your peak-picked datasets, and then align the peaks from all the other datasets to that list of peaks.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Export MSImageSet to imzML
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have added experimental support for writing imzML in Cardinal version  >= 1.11.2. It is currently available on Github (use package devtools and devtools::install_github to install from Github). It may take a couple days for the build to propagate on devel BioC.

I haven't yet tested it with other software, so I am not 100% sure of the validity of the imzML files, but it should include the most important metadata that other software would care about for importing. Let me know if you encounter problems.

Note that the conversion is lossy with regard to the metadata, because not all imzML tags are supported. The necessary intensity, m/z, and coordinate information will all be there, though.

The feature will be included with the next Bioconductor release.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Select Command
messages.body_plain:
Hi Berkley,

Unfortunately, this is a problem with RStudio. Because of the way RStudio displays plots, the graphics::locator() function that Cardinal relies on for select() has trouble updating the plot. The function will still work and return the selection correctly (although I believe you'll need to hit RStudio's "stop" button instead of ESC), but you'll have to do it "blind" as drawing the points/lines doesn't work in RStudio. It should work fine if you try it in the R application rather than RStudio.

I had hoped RStudio would fix this functionality on their own, as it is used by many more packages besides Cardinal, but I may have to think about creating a workaround at some point.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Generating 'processed' MSImageSets within R
messages.body_plain:
Hi Heath,

This will be a bit easier in the next version, as it's rather unintuitive right now. Since you ultimately need a matrix, both methods are about creating a sparse matrix from the lists of intensities and mz values.

In the current version, it's only possible if the mz data are already aligned, and somewhat awkward since the sparse matrix uses character keys to find the correct intensities:

masses <- list(c(101.1, 105.2, 107.5), c(105.2, 107.5), c(102.5, 105.2, 107.5))
intensity <- list(c(1,1,2), c(2,1), c(2,2,1))
intensity <- mapply(setNames, intensity, masses)
mz <- sort(unique(unlist(masses)))
y <- new("Hashmat", data=intensity, keys=as.character(mz), dim=c(4,3))

In more recent devel versions (matter >= 1.5.1, Cardinal >= 1.11.1), it is a little easier, and the mz data does not have to be aligned exactly:

library(matter) # make sure package:matter is in the namespace
masses <- list(c(101.1, 105.2, 107.5), c(105.2, 107.5), c(102.5, 105.2, 107.5))
intensity <- list(c(1,1,2), c(2,1), c(2,2,1))
mz <- sort(unique(unlist(masses)))
x <- sparse_mat(list(keys=masses, values=intensity), keys=mz, combiner="sum", tolerance=0.01)

The 'mz' in both cases should be the canonical vector of mz values used for the whole dataset. In the latter case, using 'sparse_mat', they do not have to match exactly the list of mz values that match your intensities, and you can use the "combiner" and "tolerance" parameters to set how they are binned.

In both cases, you get a sparse matrix that can be used as the 'spectra' argument to an MSImageSet.

-Kylie
